definitions.explanation: An armed exchange of gunfire between opposing parties, such as police and criminals, rival groups, or soldiers. Commonly seen in news reports and action films.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}と{銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}になった。
examples.english: A shootout broke out with the police.

examples.japanese: {銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}の{末|すえ}、{犯人|はんにん}は{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: After a gun battle, the suspect was arrested.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{終盤|しゅうばん}で{派手|はで}な{銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}のシーンがあった。
examples.english: There was a flashy shootout scene toward the end of the movie.

notes:
Compound of {銃撃|じゅうげき} (shooting with a gun) + {戦|せん} (battle). Used for any exchange of gunfire involving two or more parties, whether in real events such as police operations and wars or in fictional action scenes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}になる: to turn into a shootout
- {銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}が{起|お}きる: a gunfight breaks out
- {激|はげ}しい{銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}: an intense gun battle
- {銃撃戦|じゅうげきせん}の{末|すえ}: after a gun battle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {銃撃|じゅうげき}: shooting (with a gun) — the act of shooting, not necessarily a two-sided exchange
- {発砲|はっぽう}: firing a gun — a single instance of firing, used in news reports
- {戦闘|せんとう}: combat; battle — broader term covering any armed fighting
